items.headline: U.S. Markets Mixed as Investors Await Fed Decision and Monitor Earnings
items.summary: U.S. stock futures showed mixed movements early Wednesday as market participants braced for the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision later today. This follows a Tuesday session where the Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 closed higher, driven by robust corporate earnings and declining energy prices, while the Nasdaq Composite ended in negative territory due to a continued sell-off in chip stocks. Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, leading to a rise in oil prices, and the ongoing earnings season remain key factors influencing market sentiment.

items.headline: Bloom Energy Surges on Strong Q2 Results
items.summary: Bloom Energy ($BE) jumped 11% in early trading after the fuel cell maker reported record second-quarter results, surpassing both revenue and earnings expectations and raising its full-year outlook.

items.headline: Federal Reserve's FOMC Meeting Concludes Today, Rates Expected to Hold Steady
items.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) concludes its two-day meeting today, July 29, 2026. The committee is widely anticipated to keep its benchmark interest rate unchanged in the range of 3.50% to 3.75% for the fifth consecutive meeting, with the announcement due at 2 p.m. ET, followed by Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference at 2:30 p.m. ET. However, futures markets indicate a non-trivial chance of a hike and some analysts expect potential rate hikes later this year due to persistent inflation concerns.

items.headline: Sector Rotation Sees Healthcare, Communication Services, and Consumer Staples Lead
items.summary: On Tuesday, Health Care (XLV), Communication Services (XLC), and Consumer Staples (XLP) were the strongest performing sectors, gaining 2.4%, 1.9%, and 2% respectively. Conversely, Information Technology (XLK) and Energy (XLE) were the worst performers, falling 1.8% and 1.4% respectively. This indicates a broader market rotation as investors move away from chip stocks and into more defensive assets.

items.headline: Consumer Confidence Declines in July
items.summary: The Conference Board reported on Tuesday that consumer confidence dropped to 90.8 in July from an upwardly revised 92.2 in the prior month, missing consensus estimates.

items.headline: Major Earnings Boost Dow and S&P; Big Tech Reports Awaited
items.summary: Robust earnings reports from several major companies drove positive movement in the Dow and S&P 500. The Boeing Company ($BA) jumped 4.8% despite a wider-than-expected loss, exceeding revenue estimates. The Coca-Cola Company ($KO) rose 5% after beating earnings expectations, and The Sherwin-Williams Company ($SHW) surged 8.3% on strong quarterly results. Later today, tech giants Microsoft ($MSFT) and Meta Platforms ($META) are scheduled to release their quarterly earnings, alongside reports from SoFi Technologies ($SOFI), Qualcomm ($QCOM), Robinhood Markets ($HOOD), Starbucks ($SBUX), ARM Holdings ($ARM), and Nebius Group ($NBIS).

items.headline: Oil Prices Jump Amid Renewed Middle East Tensions
items.summary: Oil prices are on the rise again due to renewed hostilities in the Middle East, with Brent crude leaping 5.6% to over US$86 per barrel. This surge in energy costs contributes to broader inflation concerns and could influence future Federal Reserve policy decisions.
